---
name: read-ruling
description: Use before you decide anything an earlier ruling (an ADR) might govern, whenever a task cites a ruling, and before you write down new information. Explains how to read a ruling at an exact commit and where each kind of new information belongs.

# read-ruling

## Read the ruling before you decide

Rulings are ADR files: `docs/adr/` in this repository and `../mira-decisions/docs/adr/` in the decision log. A ruling binds later work only while its Status says it is in force.

1. List the rulings: `ls docs/adr ../mira-decisions/docs/adr`. Open the ones whose title bears on your question.
2. Pin the version you read: `git -C <repo> rev-parse HEAD` gives the full commit id. Read the ruling at that commit: `git -C <repo> show <commit>:docs/adr/<file>`.
3. Read the Status line, the first non-blank line under `## Status`:
   - `Accepted`: in force.
   - `Superseded by NNNN`: not in force. Read NNNN and use that one.
   - `Proposed` or `Deprecated`: not in force. Tell the user instead of acting on it.
4. When a task cites a ruling (repository, ADR number, commit, digest), compute the digest of what you can read: `git -C <repo> show <commit>:<path> | shasum -a 256` and compare it with the cited `sha256:<hex>`. If they differ, stop and report both values. If they match but Status is not `Accepted`, stop and report which ruling is in force.
5. A ruling is not permission to act, and an agent never edits an existing ruling.

## Where new information goes

Not everything you learn belongs in an ADR. Pick the home by who will rely on it:

| Information | Home | Who writes it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A direction that spans repos; a life, career or finance ruling that has no engineering repo | The decision space, `../mira-decisions/docs/adr/`: draft a new numbered ADR file there (never edit an existing one) | You draft; Mira confirms and merges it by pull request |
| A product rule, limit or direction inside one engineering repo that will constrain later work | A new numbered ADR in that repo's `docs/adr/` | You write the file; the coordinator confirms it |
| A trade-off that matters only to the one task | The task file (`tasks/TASK-NNN.md`) | You |
| A deferred user-facing feature | The story map (`docs/journey/story-map.md`) | You, in its Deferred section |
| How agents should work in a repository | `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` | Mira, or you with her agreement |
| Your own notes and hunches | `.agent/notes.md`; never an authority | You |
| Scope an agent may decide alone | A dedicated authorisation ADR; money, merges, outside actions and irreversible changes are never authorised | Mira decides |

Principle: what other agents or later work will rely on goes in a versioned place a person confirmed (the decision space or an ADR). What affects only the current task stays in the task. What describes how to work goes in the instruction file. Do not turn every piece of information into an ADR.

# 11. Reports are exported as CSV only

Date: 2026-09-05

## Status

Accepted

## Context

The decision came up on 2026-09-05; the people involved needed one rule to point at.

## Decision

**Words:** 「CSV only; I will not maintain a second export format.」 — Mira Example, 2026-09-05

**Options considered:**
- the export feature produces csv only (chosen)
- leave it undecided — rejected: the question keeps coming back

**Recommended:** the chosen option.

The export feature produces CSV only. No XLSX, PDF or other format is added until this record is superseded.

## Consequences

Later work follows this rule until a newer record supersedes it.
